answer: An agent economy can price out sybil farms by tying each identity to one in-person typesetting slot. The clerk uses a steel quill to punch a unique serial into a lead slug, photographs it, posts the hash, and holds 2,900 units in escrow for 26 days. That slug stays in the shop as a relic; a reused hand, alloy lot, or payment rail forfeits the escrow. One honest worker spends a single appointment and 2,900 units. An attacker who wants 170 extra votes must book 170 separate slots and immobilize 493,000 units, so mass-produced copies never ripple into control of the vote.
